record.paper_title: Kirby diagrams, trisections and gems of PL 4-manifolds: relationships, results and open problems
record.original_question: Can one design an algorithm that converts generalized Kirby diagrams with non-orientable 1-handles into gems (5-colored graph encodings of PL 4-manifolds), and can this be done in a way that yields gem-induced trisections for the resulting graphs? If so, this would extend the gem-based estimation of trisection genus from the orientable setting to all closed 4-manifolds, including non-orientable ones.

evidence.quote: As regards Section 3.1, an interesting development would be to obtain an algorithmic procedure to pass from Kirby diagrams to gems in the generalized case of diagrams representing also non-orientable 1-handles (according to [19]). If the resulting gems admitted gem-induced trisections (as happens in the orientable setting: see Theorem 17), in virtue of the non-orientable version of Laudenbach-Poenaru’s result due to [32], an estimation of the trisection genus for all closed 4-manifolds would be obtained, via gems.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

(1) A generalized Kirby diagram is a framed link diagram in S^3 in which some components are designated as "1-handle components" (drawn with a dotted/circled notation) and the rest are framed 2-handle attaching circles. In the generalized version, 1-handle components are allowed to be either orientable or non-orientable, so that the associated handle decomposition (one 0-handle, the prescribed 1-handles attached along the 1-handle components, and 2-handles attached along the framed components, completed by 3- and 4-handles in the closed case) can produce any closed (possibly non-orientable) PL 4-manifold.

(2) A gem (graph-encoded manifold) of dimension 4 is a regular 5-edge-colored multigraph (G, gamma) with gamma : E(G) -> {0,1,2,3,4}, such that the simplicial complex K(G) obtained by gluing 4-simplices according to G is a closed PL 4-manifold |K(G)|. The PL 4-manifold encoded by (G, gamma) is denoted M(G).

(3) A trisection of a closed PL 4-manifold M is a decomposition M = X_1 ∪ X_2 ∪ X_3 where each X_i is a 4-dimensional 1-handlebody, pairwise intersections X_i ∩ X_j are 3-dimensional handlebodies, and X_1 ∩ X_2 ∩ X_3 is a closed surface (the central surface). The trisection genus g(M) is the minimum genus of the central surface over all trisections of M. A gem (G, gamma) is said to admit a gem-induced trisection if a trisection of M(G) can be canonically read off from the combinatorial structure of (G, gamma) (in particular yielding an explicit upper bound on g(M(G)) in terms of combinatorial invariants of G).

Problem. Design an algorithm that, given any generalized Kirby diagram D (allowing both orientable and non-orientable 1-handle components) representing a closed PL 4-manifold M(D), produces a 5-colored gem (G_D, gamma_D) encoding M(D), in such a way that (G_D, gamma_D) admits a gem-induced trisection. Equivalently: extend the orientable gem-to-trisection construction to all closed (orientable or non-orientable) PL 4-manifolds, thereby obtaining a uniform combinatorial upper bound on the trisection genus of every closed 4-manifold via gems.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature explicitly poses this as an open development. The 2025 survey "Kirby diagrams, trisections and gems of PL 4-manifolds: relationships, results and open problems" lists the algorithmic passage from generalized (non-orientable) Kirby diagrams to gems with gem-induced trisections as an open problem. Related work (Casali–Cristofori on Kirby diagrams to 5-colored graphs, and Casali–Cristofori on gem-induced trisections from colored triangulations) handles the orientable case and partial extensions, but a full algorithmic solution covering non-orientable 1-handles together with gem-induced trisections does not appear to be established.

status_evidence.title: Kirby diagrams, trisections and gems of PL 4-manifolds: relationships, results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems on relationships between Kirby diagrams, trisections, and gems for PL 4-manifolds, including extension to non-orientable case.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of algorithmically converting generalized Kirby diagrams with non-orientable 1-handles to gems with gem-induced trisections is posed as open.

status_evidence.title: Trisections of PL 4-Manifolds Arising from Colored Triangulations
status_evidence.snippet: Extends gem-induced trisections from colored triangulations, addressing both orientable and non-orientable settings in part.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists on gem-induced trisections in the non-orientable setting via colored triangulations, but not via an algorithm starting from generalized Kirby diagrams.

status_evidence.title: Kirby diagrams and 5-colored graphs representing compact 4-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithm constructing 5-colored graphs from Kirby diagrams in the standard setting.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the orientable-case algorithm whose extension to non-orientable 1-handles is the open problem.
